summary: This lecture reaches the climax of the Isra' and Mi'raj: the Prophet ﷺ passes Sidrat al-Muntaha, where Jibril AS stops, meets Allah SWT and receives the prayer. The ustaz discusses whether the Prophet saw Allah, drawing on the views of Aisha RA, Ibn Abbas RA and the hadith of Abu Dharr RA, then explains the negotiation from fifty prayers to five with Prophet Musa AS. The second half links prayer to the crises of modern society: loneliness, burnout and achievement culture, drawing on two books and several documentaries, and explains how prayer reconnects people with Allah, with one another and with nature.
keyPoints: Jibril AS stopped at Sidrat al-Muntaha. The dramatic farewell dialogue has no strong source.
Scholars differ on whether the verse 'two bow-lengths' refers to Jibril or to the Prophet's nearness to Allah. This is a recognised difference of opinion.
Aisha RA denied that the Prophet saw Allah, and named three things no one may claim: seeing Allah with the eyes, knowing tomorrow, hiding revelation.
The safer position: the Prophet met Allah, but it is not established that he saw Him with the physical eye. How it happened is unknown.
Prayer was made obligatory at 50 times, reduced to 5 after Prophet Musa AS advised, with the reward of 50.
Prayer is the pillar of religion and a remedy for loneliness, burnout and the achievement society, because it connects us with Allah, people and nature.

chapters.title: Teaser and opening sermon
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with a clip of the conclusion: five daily prayers with the reward of fifty, then the opening sermon and a supplication.

chapters.title: Introduction: why prayer?
chapters.summary: Episode 41 continues the part that did not fit in Episode 40. The ustaz tells of his study through several documentaries and books, and how it changed the way he values prayer.

chapters.title: Sidrat al-Muntaha: Jibril stops
chapters.summary: After the hardest point in the Prophet's ﷺ life, this is the highest. Jibril AS stops at Sidrat al-Muntaha, a boundary he cannot cross. The dramatic narration of the farewell dialogue is weak.

chapters.title: Two readings of An-Najm and a recognised difference
chapters.summary: The verse 'two bow-lengths' is read as near to Jibril or near to Allah's veil. The ustaz explains why this is a valid difference, unlike treating everything as 'just a difference of opinion'.

chapters.title: Did the Prophet ﷺ see Allah? Aisha's answer
chapters.summary: Aisha RA was asked whether the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord. Her hair stood on end first, then she denied it with Al-An'am 6:103 and Ash-Shura 42:51.

chapters.title: Three things Aisha RA denied
chapters.summary: Whoever claims the Prophet saw Allah with the physical eye, knew what would happen tomorrow, or hid part of the revelation has lied. The ustaz comments on all three with evidence and contemporary examples.

chapters.title: Ibn Abbas's view and the hadith of Abu Dharr
chapters.summary: Ibn Abbas RA held that the Prophet saw Allah with his heart. Abu Dharr RA asked the Prophet ﷺ directly and received an answer about light.

chapters.title: Scholars' conclusion and seeing Allah in Paradise
chapters.summary: Seeing Allah with the physical eye is not firmly established. The Prophet met Allah, but how cannot be determined. The people of Paradise will see Allah, the greatest of all blessings.

chapters.title: The legislation of prayer: 50 to 5
chapters.summary: The Bukhari and Muslim hadith of the Prophet going up and down between Musa AS and Allah SWT until fifty prayers became five with the reward of fifty. The ustaz compares two wordings.

chapters.title: The place of prayer in Islam
chapters.summary: Prayer is the pillar of religion. The ustaz reads the hadiths of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Jabir ibn Abdillah and the covenant hadith on abandoning prayer, and explains the scholars' views.

chapters.title: The loneliness crisis and the burnout society
chapters.summary: Two books the ustaz read that week, and documentaries on Japan and Korea: lonely deaths, suicide, hikikomori, and a society that measures life by achievement.

chapters.title: Prayer as a remedy: ties to the Creator, people and nature
chapters.summary: Prayer binds us to Allah in every circumstance, to nature through the sun, moon and ablution, and to people through congregation and Friday prayer.

chapters.title: The danger of materialism, and prayer with zakat
chapters.summary: A study of children exposed to advertising, the story of an imam in Kelantan, and why prayer is always paired with zakat so that we do not become a self-absorbed society.

chapters.title: Conclusion and social impact
chapters.summary: Prayer on autopilot loses its meaning. The ustaz sums up the episode's message and invites us to organise our schedule around prayer times.

chapters.title: Closing: Prophet Musa AS, books and a supplication
chapters.summary: Even Prophet Musa AS, who spoke directly with Allah, was commanded to pray in order to remember Him. The ustaz names two books for the next two weeks and teaches a supplication after prayer.

books.context: Thesis: society has become an 'achievement society' that measures life by accomplishment, so that the poor and weak are pushed aside. The ustaz says the author is a Korean-born philosopher now in Germany, and that he also heard an Islamic philosopher comment on this book.
books.note: The author's name is not given in the lecture; added from publication details.

books.context: About 400 to 500 pages. The author studies the causes of depression and anxiety and lists nine kinds of disconnection: from purpose, from other people, from nature and from the values of a good life, among others. The experiment on children and toy advertising comes from this book.
On hikikomori, extreme work culture and 'death from overwork' in Japan, Korea and Singapore.
Source of the Mi'raj hadith, Aisha RA's denial and the discussion of prayer being reduced from 50 to 5.
Source of the Mi'raj hadith, Abu Dharr RA and Jabir ibn Abdillah RA.
Source of the covenant hadith on abandoning prayer, graded sahih by hadith scholars.
A commentary on Sahih Bukhari that discusses the Mi'raj hadith and the difference over whether the Prophet saw Allah.
Imam An-Nawawi is named by the ustaz as one of the scholars who discussed this. His commentary suits the hadith of Abu Dharr and that of Aisha RA.
Ibn Kathir is named by the ustaz as one of the scholars who discussed this difference. See his tafsir of Surah An-Najm 53:1-18.
A complete sirah summary, including the Isra' and Mi'raj in the late Meccan phase.

people.context: Denied that the Prophet saw Allah with the physical eye, citing Al-An'am 6:103 and Ash-Shura 42:51, and warned of three things that must not be claimed about the Prophet.

people.role: Companion, cousin of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Held that the Prophet saw Allah with his heart. The ustaz mentions that his father, Al-Abbas, was the Prophet's uncle.
Asked the Prophet ﷺ directly whether he saw his Lord.
Narrator of the hadith that prayer is the pillar of religion.
Narrator of the hadith that what separates a person from shirk and kufr is abandoning prayer.
Both narrated the Mi'raj hadith and the reduction of prayer.
Narrated the covenant hadith about prayer.

people.role: Founder of a school of law
people.context: The main position in our community: a person who abandons prayer out of laziness or neglect, without denying that it is obligatory, does not leave Islam.
Mentioned briefly as a scholar who discussed the hadith of Abu Dharr and the question of seeing Allah. The ustaz does not wish to dwell on it.
Asked Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to go back and request a reduction of prayers. The ustaz sees him as a caring agent and adviser to the Prophet Muhammad's community.
Met by the Prophet ﷺ in the seventh heaven, leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur.
Author of two books the ustaz read to understand the crisis of loneliness and exhaustion in modern society.

lessons.title: Be courteous when speaking of Allah's Essence
lessons.body: Aisha RA did not answer yes or no. She began with her hair standing on end in fear and awe. The ustaz notes that the Companions also did not ask much about Allah's Essence.

lessons.title: Respect recognised differences, but not 'everything is a difference of opinion'
lessons.body: A valid difference exists when both sides have strong evidence. We choose one view and respect the other. It is different from treating every matter as open to disagreement.

lessons.title: The Prophet ﷺ did not know the unseen except by revelation
lessons.body: So claims to know what will happen tomorrow, like fortune-tellers and shamans, are deception that exploits people's ignorance. Even the Prophet ﷺ did not know what was in people's hearts.

lessons.title: The Prophet ﷺ did not hide any revelation
lessons.body: Beware of groups that claim secret rituals or paths taught only to a select few. The ustaz mentions his own experience of joining such a group.

lessons.title: Be careful attributing things to Allah and His Messenger
lessons.body: When we say 'Islam teaches this', we are referring to Allah and His Messenger. If it is not from them, we are lying in their name.

lessons.title: Our conduct can give the lie to the Prophet's ﷺ message
lessons.body: Even if our tongue does not lie, our actions can make people see Islam and prayer as the cause of problems rather than the solution.

lessons.title: Allah's mercy: five prayers, the reward of fifty
lessons.body: The minimum time for the maximum reward. Prophet Musa AS also showed great concern for the community of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, even though that community would enter Paradise before his own.

lessons.title: Prayer is the pillar that holds up religion
lessons.body: Without a pole, a tent is just cloth. Prayer holds up every other part of life.

lessons.title: Prayer keeps our relationships: with the Creator, people and nature
lessons.body: We are never cut off from Allah in any circumstance. Congregational and Friday prayers bring us together with people of every background. Prayer times follow the sun, and ablution and cleanliness link us with nature.

lessons.title: Don't become a society that only chases achievement
lessons.body: When life is measured only by achievement, the weak and the poor are pushed aside. That is why prayer is always paired with zakat.

lessons.title: Don't make prayer a place to elevate yourself
lessons.body: Prayer is where we bow. Don't leave the mosque more arrogant than you entered, and don't wrap your ego in religious terms and behaviour.

lessons.title: One caring act changes more than many lectures
lessons.body: The story of an imam in Kelantan who collected money for a neighbour who never came to the mosque, until the man wept. From it the ustaz stresses that worship must make us more alert to others' hardship.

lessons.title: Take the good from the East, and learn quickly from their mistakes
lessons.body: The ustaz mentions the Look East Policy (1982), and advises us not to be 'late adopters' who follow a path already proven painful. Have no sense of inferiority, because prayer reached us 'free'.

lessons.title: Keep prayer alive so it doesn't become autopilot
lessons.body: Prayer that becomes habit without meaning loses its effect. Arrange your schedule around prayer times and think about how to care for each prayer.

lessons.title: Pray to remember Allah, because we forget easily
lessons.body: Prophet Musa AS spoke directly with Allah, yet was still commanded to pray in order to remember Him. The five prayers reset our compass throughout the day.

glossary.meaning: The lote tree at the boundary of the seventh heaven, the limit no angel may pass, including Jibril AS.
The Kaaba in the seventh heaven. Every day 70,000 angels circle it and do not return.
A difference of scholarly opinion that is accepted, because both sides have strong evidence.
A veil or barrier. Here, the veil of Allah's majesty and the way Allah speaks to people.
The heart. Ibn Abbas RA said the Prophet saw Allah with the fu'ad, meaning with the heart, not the physical eye.
A hadith narrated by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim, the highest level of authenticity.
The title of Prophet Musa AS, meaning the one who spoke directly with Allah.
A term from The Burnout Society: a society that measures the value of life by achievement, so that the weak and those needing help are seen as obstacles.
The phenomenon of young people in Japan who shut themselves in at home for years.
'The best of servants'. The ustaz invites us to aspire to this rank with Allah, not worldly status.

dalil.context: A verse read in two ways: Jibril drew near to the Prophet, or the Prophet drew near to the veil of Allah's majesty.
dalil.translation: and then approached––coming down

dalil.context: The picture of the closest nearness. According to the ustaz, the Prophet's position was 'at the closest range'.
dalil.translation: until he was two bow-lengths away or even closer––

dalil.context: Ibn Abbas RA took this verse as evidence that the Prophet saw Allah with his heart (fu'ad).
dalil.translation: [The Prophet’s] own heart did not distort what he saw.

dalil.context: In the same passage Ibn Abbas RA held that the Prophet saw 'a second time' with his heart. Aisha RA interpreted it as Jibril AS.
dalil.translation: A second time he saw him:

dalil.context: Recited by Aisha RA after saying that whoever claims the Prophet saw Allah has lied.
dalil.translation: No vision can take Him in, but He takes in all vision. He is the All Subtle, the All Aware.

dalil.context: Recited by Aisha RA: Allah speaks to people through revelation, from behind a veil, or by sending an angel.
dalil.translation: It is not granted to any mortal that God should speak to him except through revelation or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal by His command what He will: He is exalted and wise.

dalil.context: Recited by Aisha RA to reject the claim that the Prophet ﷺ knew what would happen tomorrow. The ustaz cites 'no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow'.
dalil.translation: Knowledge of the Hour [of Resurrection] belongs to God; it is He who sends down the relieving rain and He who knows what is hidden in the womb. No soul knows what it will reap tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die; it is God who is all knowing and all aware.

dalil.context: Recited by Aisha RA to reject the claim that the Prophet ﷺ hid part of the revelation.
dalil.translation: Messenger, proclaim everything that has been sent down to you from your Lord- if you do not, then you will not have communicated His message- and God will protect you from people. God does not guide those who defy Him.

dalil.context: The verse number is not mentioned. Identified from the story of Prophet Musa AS asking to see Allah, after which the mountain crumbled and he fainted.
dalil.translation: When Moses came for the appointment, and his Lord spoke to him, he said, ‘My Lord, show Yourself to me: let me see You!’ He said, ‘You will never see Me, but look at that mountain: if it remains standing firm, you will see Me,’ and when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble: Moses fell down unconscious. When he recovered, he said, ‘Glory be to You! To You I turn in repentance! I am the first to believe!’

dalil.context: The verse number is not mentioned. The ustaz mentions Surah Taha and Allah's dialogue with Musa AS about what was in his hand.
dalil.translation: ‘Moses, what is that in your right hand?’

dalil.context: 'Establish prayer for My remembrance.' Even Prophet Musa was commanded to pray so that he would always remember Allah.
dalil.translation: I am God; there is no god but Me. So worship Me and keep up the prayer so that you remember Me.

dalil.context: Read in full by the ustaz. There are two wordings: one says it was reduced by half, the other says 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, then 5.
dalil.translation: Allah made fifty prayers obligatory each day and night, reduced until five, yet the reward remains fifty. 'My decree does not change.'

dalil.context: The ustaz explains that 'lied' here means erred in reporting, not deliberately deceived.
dalil.translation: Whoever tells you that Muhammad ﷺ saw his Lord has certainly lied.

dalil.context: This is Ibn Abbas's RA interpretation, not a clear statement of the Prophet ﷺ. This is the source of the difference.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ saw Allah with his heart.

dalil.context: The only report where the Prophet was asked directly, but its meaning needs scholarly discussion.
dalil.translation: The Prophet replied: 'He is light; how could I see Him?' In another narration: 'I saw light.'

dalil.context: The ustaz explains with the analogy of a Bedouin tent: without a pole, a tent is just cloth.
dalil.translation: The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its peak is jihad in the way of Allah.

dalil.context: The ustaz cites Imam Ash-Shafi'i's view: abandoning it out of laziness while not denying that it is obligatory does not take a person out of Islam.
dalil.translation: What separates a person from shirk and kufr is abandoning prayer.

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses it means abandoning it deliberately and not believing it is obligatory.
dalil.translation: The covenant between us and them is prayer. Whoever abandons it has disbelieved.

dalil.context: Mentioned in the context of being careful about attributing things to Allah and His Messenger.
dalil.translation: Whoever lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.

dalil.context: Recited before the salam in the final tashahhud, or after the salam.
dalil.translation: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well.

sirah.era: Late Meccan phase, before the Hijra
sirah.summary: This episode sits at the climax of the Isra' and Mi'raj, after the series of heavy trials in earlier episodes. The ustaz does not give an exact date in this lecture.

events.label: Before
events.title: The lowest point in the Prophet's ﷺ life
events.desc: The ustaz recalls that the sirah has its most critical phase. In this series it includes the episodes on the deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib, and the Ta'if incident.

events.label: Journey
events.title: From Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa, then the first to the seventh heaven
events.desc: A recap of the previous episode: the Prophet met Prophet Ibrahim AS leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, where 70,000 angels circle and do not return.

events.label: Sidrat al-Muntaha
events.title: Jibril stops; the Prophet ﷺ enters where no angel goes
events.desc: The point of parting between the Prophet ﷺ and Jibril AS. Jibril cannot pass that limit.

events.label: Meeting
events.title: Meeting Allah SWT and receiving the prayer
events.desc: The peak of the greatest meeting, accompanied by the law that became the core of life: fifty prayers each day and night.

events.label: Back and forth
events.title: Negotiating with Prophet Musa AS in the sixth heaven
events.desc: The Prophet ﷺ went down, met Musa AS, went up again, repeatedly, until five prayers with the reward of fifty.

events.label: After
events.title: Next episodes: Prayer as the core of life's balance, and the heavenly journey denied
events.desc: According to this series' list, episodes 42 and 43 continue the discussion of prayer and the Quraysh's rejection of the journey.

mindmap.label: Prayer: the greatest gift from the Mi'raj
mindmap.detail: The Prophet's ﷺ meeting with Allah at the Mi'raj gave rise to the prayer, and prayer is the remedy for modern people's crisis of disconnection.
